newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News-Jan 20.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News-Jan 20.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)

THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW Federal Cabinet is expected to endorse a plan by Industry Minister John Moore next month which would see Commonwealth outlays to the pharmaceuticals sector cut by 40 per cent, saving nearly A$60 million in annual Budget outlays. However, in a concession o industry, Moore will recommend that pharmaceutical manufacturers receive a greater period of patent exclusivity to develop new drugs. Page 1.

A flood of small investors' money to US mutual funds may lead to a greater flow of mutual fund cash to Australia, with recent surveys by Merill Lynch indicating that US investors are optimistic about the US-dollar-sensitive economies in the Pacific and Lain America and that is where they are investing.
Page 1.

In response to a Sydney newspaper report that the Federal Government was considering raising the age at which superannuation could be accessed from 55 to 60, a spokesman for Assistant Treasurer Rod Kemp said the Government was not prepared to comment on what may or may not be in the May Federal Budget. Page 2.

Only two weeks after Ford Australia was declared market leader in 1996 for the second consecutive year, the car maker announced it would shut one of its Broadmeadows assembly lines and parts of its Geelong foundry and stamping operations on February 11 an 12 and March 11 and 12 after a drop in sales of its locally made products in 1996 led to an unacceptable stock build-up. Page 4.

In his 1996 report to Parliament, New South Wales Auditor-General Tony Harris, called for a review of the generous superannuation scheme for New South Wales members of Parliament and criticised the "golden handcuffs" being paid to staff of Axiom Funds Mangement to try to minimise staff turnover. Page 15.

After undergoing a massive restructuring, AWA Ltd will this year launch an attack on the Australian gambling market, with plans to buy the New South Wales Totaliser Agency Board and pursue an aggressive expansion of its Club Keno game.
AWA is also hoping to accelerate the growth of its poker machine business, with the A$140 million acquisition of Melbourne-based Olympic. Page 15.

While there is speculation that Crown Ltd could acquire the management rights of the Crown Casino in Melbourne from Hudson Conway to prepare for links with the Sydney Harbour Casino, Crown sources say Crown and SHC would have to settle several issues withState Governments and casino regulators before making any moves. Page 17.

Despite analysts downgrading its profit outlook by as much as 20 per cent, Burns Philp & Co Ltd company secretary George McLean told the Australian Stock Exchange on Friday that the company had no reason to expect its operating profit before abnormal item and tax to vary by more than 15 per cent. Page 17.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Federal Government's Export Finance and Insurance Corp board has retained the services of Arthur Anderson Corporate Finance and The Allen Consulting Group's Vince FitzGerald to assist it in a wide-ranging strategic review that should be completed soon FitzGerald will act as an interface between the board and the Government, while Arthur Anderson is examining the business itself and will complete a full commercial assessment.
Page 17.

An alliance has been formed between Australia's biggest home-grown sports marketing group, Sports Marketing and Management, and the Asia Sport Group, in a bid to meet the rising demand for sport in Asia. The group also intends to tap into the opportunitis arising from the Sydney 2000 Olympics. Page 17.

After holding extensive talks with the Mapoon and Napranum Aboriginal communities and the Cape York Land Council, Alcan Aluminium Ltd is close to finalising a native title pact outside the right-to negotiate process dictated by the Native Title Act. Alcan needs to use land which Napranum Deed of Grant in Trust land in order to build a port facility and an access road leading to the proposed 2.5 million tonne a year Ely bauxite mine north of Weipa. Page 19.

Analysts believe North Ltd is set to close a deal to buy 58 per cent of an eastern Canada company which produces 10 million tonnes of lump and pellet iron ore a year. While, a spokesman for North said the company was looking at several operations, he refused to comment more specifically. Page 19.

According to a study by the Centre for Agricultural and Regional Economics, based at the University of New England in northern New South Wales, as many as 28 ethanol plants, each with a capacity to produce 50 million litres a year, could be established in regional centres, boosting the economy of rural New South Wales by up to A$1.1 billion a year. Page 19.

According to research commissioned by the Australian Stock Exchange in its supplementary submission to the Wallis inquiry, problems faced by SMEs would be eased if prospectus requirements in the Corporations Law were addressed and changes were made to onus of proof provisions, forecast requirements and there was a source and application of funds table in all prospectuses. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian companies such as Lend Lease and Brambles Industries may not bid for the A$3 billion sale of Australia's airports because of concerns over Australia's foreign ownership rules. Under the Foreign Takeovers Act, some major Australian listed compaies with a handful of foreign shareholders could be deemed a foreign entity, and then, under the Airports Act 1996, a 49 per cent ceiling on foreign ownership is placed on any company operating an Australian airport. Page 33.

Following a long meeting on Friday, Reef Casino Trust manager, Reef Corporate Services, agreed to allow the trust's adviser, Grant Samuel and Associates, to seek fresh capital. Formal documentation is expected later in the week, when complete details of he reorganisation are also expected. Page 33.

As Wall Street hit a record of 6,833.10 on Friday, Australian shares are expected to hit new highs this week. However, market makers will delay any big moves until after Tuesday, when United States Federal Reserve chairman Dr Alan Greenspan addresses a Snate Budget Committee meeting, where he will discuss the health of the United States economy. Page 33.

The Australian Stock Exchange supplementary submission to the Wallis committee into Australia's financial system has called for a radical reform of the Corporations Law and the fund-raising provisions of the prospectus regulations to better protect sharehlders. Page 35.

Following concerns that the Consumer Price Index is not a suitable measure of inflation, the Australian Bureau of Statistics is considering radical changes to the index, including releasing figures each month and producing two separate measures. Page 35.

Federal Opposition acting treasury spokesman Mark Latham yesterday warned of an across the board increase in bank fees and charges following the ANZ Bank's announcement last week of increased fees as part of a sweeping overhaul of its transaction accounts. Latham called on Federal Treasurer Peter Costello to order formal price monitoring of the bank charges by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission. Page 35.
THE AGE

A survey released yesterday in the latest edition of the ANZ Bank's Investment Monitor showed that Australian shares were where the smart investment money was last year, with shares yielding a 14.6 per cent return in the 12 months to December 31, figures that outstripped other asset classes significantly in that period. Page C1.

One of Australia's last independent broking firms, McIntosh Securities, will today merge with Wall Street giant Merrill Lynch & Co, forming a new force on the stockbroking scene. The new entity would be known as Merrill Lynch (Australia) Pty Ltd, and themerger will end 25 years of the McIntosh name being known in the stockbroking industry. Page C1.

New Yorker Darian Braun moved to Melbourne with his Australian wife three years ago, and purchased Bucket-O-Meat, a Dandenong firm that specialises in quality fresh dog food that is cooked daily and home delivered. With pet food being one of the top 10 cnsumer categories bought in supermarkets, Braun is trying to take on the players in a A$760 million a year industry. Page C3.

Woolworths managing director Reg Clairs says the retailer, which surprised the market last week with a strong first-half sales result, would look into the possibility of a goods and services tax. Clairs' comments follow the release of a survey by the Ausralian Chamber of Commerce and Industry that showed the tax regime was the biggest constraint to investment. Page C3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
